stimulus.text:
The engraving shows armed farmers fleeing through a village street in Springfield, Massachusetts, as uniformed troops with a cannon advance behind them. The farmers, many carrying muskets, run past bare winter trees and a white house. The artist's signature, “C. Kendrick,” appears at the lower right.
— C. Kendrick, Shays's forces fleeing troops at Springfield, c. 1902 (from a 1902 publication)

stem: Historians often cite Shays's Rebellion (1786–1787) as a significant event in United States history because it

options.text: proved that the new national government could enforce its laws with federal troops
options.misconception: Background: that was the Whiskey Rebellion of 1794, under the Constitution, not Shays's Rebellion.

options.text: made many Americans decide that slavery could not last
options.misconception: Background: Shays's Rebellion was about taxes and debts in Massachusetts, not about slavery.

options.text: showed the government under the Articles could not stop an armed uprising
proved that farmers supported a stronger national government
options.misconception: Background: the farmers fought the government; it was their opponents who wanted a stronger national government.

rationales.C: Background from the books: Congress had no power to raise an army, so Massachusetts had to put the rebellion down with its own militia, which exposed the national government's weakness.
rationales.A: Background: enforcing laws with federal troops came later, when Washington crushed the Whiskey Rebellion in 1794.
rationales.B: Background: the rebellion was about taxes, debts, and foreclosures in western Massachusetts, not slavery.
rationales.D: Background: the farmers fought the government; the call for a stronger government came from men like Washington and Hamilton.
rationales.general:
1. Name the event. Western Massachusetts farmers took up arms against taxes and foreclosures.
2. Background: Congress under the Articles could not raise an army to help.
3. Background: Massachusetts raised its own militia, so the rebellion exposed a national weakness.
4. Background: national leaders read the failure as proof the Articles had to be replaced.
Remember: Shays matters because the national government could only watch.
